note: Re-judged against current committed source. RFC 3101 Section 2.4 requires NSSA border routers to originate a default into every directly attached NSSA; Sections 2.4 and 2.7 distinguish regular Type-7 defaults from no-summary Type-3 defaults. TestOSPFNSSABorderRouterDefaultsEveryArea configures backbone plus regular and no-summary NSSAs, calls applyNSSADefaults, and requires the regular area's default LSID. TestOSPFNSSANoSummaryDefaultInjection exercises OriginateSummaries and requires the actual no-summary default LSA and decoded metric. TestOSPFNSSAType3SummaryImport independently distinguishes the regular and no-summary policy results. TestOSPFv3NSSABorderRouterOriginatesDefault requires the 0x2007 NSSA-LSA with a zero-length prefix through the shared reconciler. applyNSSADefaults iterates configured attached NSSAs; wantsType7Default grants the ABR default without an operator gate, while OriginateSummaries supplies the no-summary default. Removing either producer branch fails its positive assertion. TestOSPFNSSAInternalRouterOriginatesNoBorderDefault is the clean non-ABR applicability control. The additional v3 internal-router negative lacks a usable forwarding address, so it is not credited as an independent discriminator for this requirement. checkNSSADefault still waits for Full and requires the exact selected, destination-selected, installed OSPF default and its active FIB next hop in one FRR route entry through requireRouteInstalledVia. Its new removal of Docker's competing default restores that topology without relaxing the assertion. Its new first-epoch capture is additive: finish joins nativeErr with capture errors and cannot turn a failed default assertion into success. The Type-5 exclusion observation concerns a separate requirement and is not substituted for the default assertion. The unchanged unit controls plus preserved installed-route assertion enforce this requirement. This audit is a source rejudgment, not a new runtime or mutation result.
